kind: assumed inputs for a synthetic model; nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository

map.name: logistic map
map.note: A textbook model chosen because every quantity in the lesson can be computed for it. It is not a model of the project.

regimes.expected_attractor: chaotic, the whole interval from 0 to 1

starting_points.draw: 0.1 + 0.8 * random.Random(seed).random(), one draw per starting point, the same draws for every regime
starting_points.note: Each drawn point is iterated settle_steps times before use, so that the pair of runs starts on the attractor.

perturbation_rule: the second run starts at x + error when x < 0.5 and at x - error otherwise, so that it stays inside the interval

cited_comparison.source: MAT-024, Dynamical Systems, Stability and Feedback, section 2, table of exponents (Demerzel commit 4b03838800dcd4894f1e026461979bff1d985ca8, state/streeling/courses/mathematics/en/mat-024-dynamical-systems-stability-feedback.md)
cited_comparison.note: These are the settings of the first block of the long orbit above, so the first block is compared with the printed value.

exponent_from_median_gaps.rule: from step 0 to the last tabulated step at which the median gap is still usable: below small_gap_limit (growth not yet slowed by the size of the attractor) and at least floor_in_spacings spacings of doubles (not yet lost in rounding)

contraction.note: Regimes whose exponent is negative: steps until an error has shrunk from initial_error to below target_error.

hypothesis_thresholds.note: Written into the research cycle's hypothesis before the first run of the fixture.

double_precision.first_difference_note: A bound set before the first run, not fitted to it. Each form rounds at most three times per step; each rounding is at most half a spacing of the doubles between 2 and 4 and reaches the result as at most 2 spacings of the doubles between 1/2 and 1. So each form is within 6 such spacings of the exact value and the two forms within 12 of each other; the bound allows 16.

beyond_the_horizon.known_share_reason: At r = 4 the substitution x = sin^2(pi * t) turns the map into t -> 2t mod 1, for which the uniform distribution of t is invariant; x < 0.25 holds for t in [0, 1/6) and (5/6, 1], a set of length 1/3.

high_precision.note: Some runs are repeated on Python integers, from the same starting doubles, to separate what belongs to the map from what belongs to double-precision arithmetic: the gap table where the exponent is negative, the two runs of beyond_the_horizon, and the horizons of the lesson's tolerance in the chaotic regimes.

agreement_with_doubles.note: A control set before the first run: where doubles still resolve the median gap, the two arithmetics must give the same number.

worked_examples.note: Inputs of the lesson's exercises that are not already listed above.

exercise_5.option_b_re_measure_every_note: the formula horizon of option B rounded down, which is what a planner who trusts the formula would choose
exercise_5.wanted_share_unit: a forecast is one run over the whole wanted span, re-measured every k steps; it counts as within tolerance only if the gap is below the tolerance at every step of the span

hand_computed_case.note: Worked by hand in the README: r = 4, first run on the fixed point 0.75, second run 2^-10 below it.

phase_error.note: In the two-cycle regime, start the second run on the other point of the cycle: an error too large to count as small.

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical delivery simulator for the learner task. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.
transfer_task.state: backlog as a share of capacity, between 0 and 1
